pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever wished you could see the future? Maybe you wanted to know who you would marry. Maybe you wanted to know what job you would have. Maybe you wanted to know what would happen tomorrow. We all want to know the future. We all want to know what is coming.


The Bible says there were people who knew the future. They were called prophets. They did not use crystal balls. They did not use tarot cards. They did not use horoscopes. They spoke for God. God told them what was coming. And they wrote it down. They wrote about a coming figure called the Messiah. They predicted His life. They predicted His death. They predicted His resurrection. They predicted everything.


These prophets lived centuries apart. They lived in different countries. They had different jobs. Isaiah was a prophet in the royal court. Micah was a prophet in the countryside. Zechariah was a prophet after the exile. They did not know each other. They did not compare notes. They did not plan their predictions together. They just spoke what God told them. And when you put their predictions together, you see a perfect picture. You see the life of Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who wants to see the future told. It is for the person who wants to understand the ancient voices. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 predictions from these ancient voices. We are going to see what they said. We are going to see how they came true. And we are going to see the one they predicted. That one is Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the prophets as old men in robes. You will see them as messengers. You will see them as voices. You will see them as witnesses. You will understand their pred...

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that changed your life? Maybe a teacher. Maybe a coach. Maybe a parent. They said something that stuck with you. They said something that shaped you. Moses was that voice for the people of Israel. He was the great deliverer. He was the great lawgiver. He was the great prophet. But Moses said there was another voice coming. Another prophet. Another deliverer. Another lawgiver. It was a prediction. It was a promise. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites, and I will put my words in his mouth. He will tell them everything I command him." - Deuteronomy 18:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was speaking to the people. He said God would raise up a prophet like him. This was a big claim. Moses was the greatest prophet in history. He was the one who parted the Red Sea. He was the one who received the Ten Commandments. He was the one who talked to God face to face. But he said someone else was coming. Someone even greater. This new prophet would speak God's words. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you must listen to everything he tells you.'" - Acts 3:22


Peter quotes this prophecy in the book of Acts. He applies it to Jesus. Jesus is the new Moses. Moses led people out of physical slavery in Egypt. Jesus leads people out of spiritual slavery to sin. Moses gave the law. Jesus gives grace. Moses spoke to God face to face. Jesus is God. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
The Jews were waiting for this prophet. They asked John the Baptist, "Are you the prophet?" They knew the prophecy. They were looking for someone like Moses. Jesus fulfilled that expectation. He was the greater Moses. The voice of Moses was not silent. It was a prediction. It was the future told.


The Resonance
We are not just looking for a teacher. We are looking for a liberator. A teacher can tell you what to do. A liberator can set you free. Jesus is both. He teaches us the truth. He sets us free from sin. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the voice of Moses. Thank you for the prediction of a greater prophet. Thank you for sending Jesus. He is the liberator. He is the deliverer. Help me to listen to Him. Help me to follow Him. Set me free from the things that hold me back. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that painted a picture? Maybe an artist. Maybe a poet. Maybe a storyteller. They used words to create a picture in your mind. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He was a prophet. He was a poet. He was a storyteller. He painted pictures of the coming Messiah. He painted pictures of a child. He painted pictures of a king. He painted pictures of a servant. He painted pictures of a savior. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah painted a picture of a child. But this was not a normal child. This was a child with titles. Wonderful Counselor. Mighty God. Everlasting Father. Prince of Peace. These are titles for God. Isaiah said the child would be God. He said the child would be born. He said the child would be given. It was a prediction. It was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I and the Father are one." - John 10:30


Jesus made a claim that shocked everyone. He said, "I and the Father are one." He was saying He is God. He was saying He is the Mighty God. He was saying He is the Everlasting Father. The religious leaders tried to kill Him for saying this. They knew what He meant. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
Isaiah painted a picture of a divine child. Jesus claimed to be divine. The picture matches. The prediction was fulfilled. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Spirituality is not just about reaching up. The Divine reached down. God did not just send a message. He sent Himself. He came in the form of a baby. He came to be with us. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are Mighty God. Thank you for coming to earth. Thank you for stepping down from heaven. Thank you for being the Everlasting Father. Help me to know you more. Help me to love you more. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice from a small town? Maybe a local hero. Maybe a local legend. They came from a place nobody expected. They came from a place nobody knew. Micah was that kind of voice. He was a prophet. He came from a small town called Moresheth. He was not from the capital. He was not from the palace. He was from the countryside. But God used him to speak. God used him to predict. God used him to tell the future. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times." - Micah 5:2 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Micah was looking at the towns of Judah. He said, "Bethlehem, you are small." Bethlehem was a small town. It was not a capital. It was not a major city. But Micah said the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem. This was a specific address. This was a specific prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem the town of David, because he belonged to the house and line of David." - Luke 2:4


Joseph and Mary lived in Nazareth. They were far from Bethlehem. But the Roman emperor Caesar Augustus ordered a census. Every person had to go to their ancestral town to register. Joseph was from the line of David. David was from Bethlehem. So Joseph traveled to Bethlehem. And Mary went with him. She gave birth in Bethlehem. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
It is statistically impossible to orchestrate your own birthplace. You cannot control where you are born. But the prophet knew. He named the town. And the Roman census made it happen. The voice of Micah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
God pays attention to details. If He cared enough to arrange the exact birthplace of His son, He cares about the details of your life. He cares about your address. He cares about your family. He cares about the small things. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, thank you for caring about details. Thank you for planning every step of your son's life. Thank you that you care about my life too. Help me to trust you with the small things. Help me to trust you with the big things. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about money? Maybe a financial advisor. Maybe a banker. Maybe a businessperson. They talk about prices. They talk about costs. They talk about value. Zechariah was that kind of voice. He was a prophet. He spoke about a price. He spoke about a cost. He spoke about a value. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"I told them, 'If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it.' So they paid me thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, 'Throw it to the potter'—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD." - Zechariah 11:12-13 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah acted out a prophecy. He played the role of the shepherd. He asked the people for his pay. They paid him thirty pieces of silver. This was a low price. It was the price of a slave. Then God told him to throw the silver to the potter. The potter was a craftsman. The silver would be used to buy a field. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then one of the Twelve—the one called Judas Iscariot—went to the chief priests and asked, 'What are you willing to give me if I deliver him over to you?' So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver." - Matthew 26:14-15


Judas went to the chief priests. He asked them how much they would pay him to betray Jesus. They counted out thirty pieces of silver. This was the exact price Zechariah predicted. Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is an incredibly specific prediction. It predicts the exact amount of money. It predicts the exact price of betrayal. Jesus was sold for thirty pieces of silver. The voice of Zechariah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Jesus allowed Himself to be valued at the price of a slave. Not because He was worth that much. But because He valued YOU that much. You are worth everything to Him. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for valuing me enough to humble yourself. Thank you for allowing yourself to be sold for thirty pieces of silver. Thank you for loving me that much. Help me to see my worth in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The Voice of Zechariah

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that sang? Maybe a singer. Maybe a songwriter. Maybe a musician. They use music to express their feelings. They use music to tell their story. David was that kind of voice. He was a king. He was a shepherd. He was a songwriter. He wrote the Psalms. He wrote about his pain. He wrote about his joy. He wrote about the Messiah. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Dogs surround me, a pack of villains encircles me; they pierce my hands and my feet." - Psalm 22:16 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He is describing a scene of suffering. He says, "Dogs surround me. A pack of villains encircles me. They pierce my hands and my feet." He is describing a person being attacked by enemies. This was a prediction. It was a prophecy. It was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So the other disciples told him, 'We have seen the Lord!' But he said to them, 'Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.'" - John 20:25


Thomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus appeared to them. He said, "Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, I will not believe." A week later, Jesus appeared again. He said to Thomas, "Put your finger here; see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side." Thomas saw the nail marks. He saw the pierced hands and feet. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
Crucifixion did not exist when David wrote this Psalm. It was invented by the Romans a thousand years later. The fact that David predicted pierced hands and feet is stunning. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The scars of Jesus are proof of His love for you. He bears those marks for eternity. He is not ashamed of them. He is not ashamed of you. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the scars you bear for me. Thank you for the nail marks in your hands. Thank you for loving me that much. Help me to never forget your sacrifice. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The Voice of David

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a new beginning? Maybe a coach. Maybe a mentor. Maybe a friend. They told you that you could start over. They told you that you could have a fresh start. Jeremiah was that kind of voice. He was a prophet. He spoke about a new covenant. He spoke about a new beginning. He spoke about a new heart. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"This is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after that time," declares the LORD. "I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people." - Jeremiah 31:33 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Jeremiah was a prophet. He was looking at the old covenant. The old covenant was written on stone. It was external. It was a list of rules. But Jeremiah said a new covenant was coming. It would be written on hearts. It would be internal. It would be a relationship. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For this reason Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance—now that he has died as a ransom to set them free from the sins committed under the first covenant." - Hebrews 9:15


Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant. He died to set us free. He wrote the law on our hearts. He made us His people. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about a new relationship. The old covenant was about rules. The new covenant is about relationship. Jesus brought the new covenant. The voice of Jeremiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Do you want a relationship with God? Do you want His law written on your heart? The new covenant is for you. Jesus made it possible. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the new covenant. Thank you for writing your law on my heart. Thank you for being my God. Thank you for making me your people. Help me to live in this new relationship. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The Voice of Jeremiah

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a servant? Maybe a servant leader. Maybe a humble hero. Maybe a sacrificial friend. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a servant. He spoke about a suffering servant. He spoke about a savior. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth." - Isaiah 53:7 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah described the suffering servant. He said the servant would be oppressed. He said the servant would be afflicted. But the servant would not open his mouth. He would be silent. He would be led like a lamb to the slaughter. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he gave no answer. Then Pilate asked him, 'Don't you hear the testimony they are bringing against you?' But Jesus made no reply, not even to a single charge—to the great amazement of the governor." - Matthew 27:12-14


Jesus was brought before Pilate. The chief priests and elders accused him. They made false charges. They lied about him. Pilate asked Jesus, "Don't you hear what they are saying?" Jesus said nothing. He did not defend himself. He was silent. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the behavior of the Messiah during his trial. He would be silent. Jesus was silent. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is be silent. Trusting God in the face of false accusations is a sign of strength. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being silent so that I could speak to God. Thank you for enduring false accusations. Help me to trust you when I am accused. Help me to be silent when I need to be. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a shepherd? Maybe a pastor. Maybe a guide. Maybe a protector. Zechariah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a shepherd. He spoke about a smitten shepherd. He spoke about scattered sheep. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is close to me! declares the LORD Almighty. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the little ones." - Zechariah 13:7 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah said the sword will strike the shepherd. The shepherd will be smitten. He will be struck down. And then the sheep will be scattered. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then Jesus told them, 'This very night you will all fall away on account of me, for it is written: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered."'" - Matthew 26:31


Jesus quoted this prophecy. He told His disciples they would all fall away. Jesus was arrested. The disciples ran away. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the disciples. They were the sheep. They would scatter. Jesus was the shepherd. He would be struck. The voice of Zechariah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Even when you fail or run away, Jesus does not abandon you. He is the Good Shepherd who goes after the scattered sheep. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for never giving up on me. Thank you for coming after me when I run away. Thank you for being the Good Shepherd. Help me to stop running. Help me to stay close to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Voice of Zechariah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about mockery? Maybe a bully. Maybe a critic. Maybe a hater. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about mockers. He spoke about insults. He spoke about shaking heads. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"All who see me mock me; they hurl insults, shaking their heads. 'He trusts in the LORD,' they say, 'let the LORD rescue him. Let him deliver him, since he delights in him.'" - Psalm 22:7-8 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David is describing the mockers. They mock him. They hurl insults. They shake their heads. They say, "He trusts in the LORD. Let the LORD rescue him." This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads and saying, 'You who are going to destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! Come down from the cross, if you are the Son of God!' In the same way the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders mocked him. 'He saved others,' they said, 'but he can't save himself! He's the king of Israel! Let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him. He trusts in God. Let God rescue him now if he wants him, for he said, "I am the Son of God."'" - Matthew 27:39-43


This is exactly what happened at the crucifixion. The people mocked Jesus. They shook their heads. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
The exact words of the mockers were predicted a thousand years before they said them. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
When people mock your faith, remember that you are in good company. Jesus faced the same thing and overcame it. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for enduring mockery for me. Thank you for not coming down from the cross. Help me to stand strong when my faith is mocked. Help me to forgive those who mock me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about thirst? Maybe a runner. Maybe a traveler. Maybe a survivor. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about thirst. He spoke about gall. He spoke about vinegar. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"They put gall in my food and gave me vinegar for my thirst." - Psalm 69:21 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He is describing his suffering. He says, "They put gall in my food and gave me vinegar for my thirst." Gall is a bitter substance. Vinegar is sour wine. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"There they offered Jesus wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, he refused to drink it. Later, knowing that everything had now been finished, and so that Scripture would be fulfilled, Jesus said, 'I am thirsty.' A jar of wine vinegar was there, so they soaked a sponge in it, put the sponge on a stalk of the hyssop plant, and lifted it to Jesus' lips." - Matthew 27:34; John 19:28-29


The soldiers offered Jesus gall and vinegar. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the smallest details of the crucifixion. Jesus experienced both. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Even in suffering, Jesus fulfilled the smallest details of prophecy. He is a God of precision and love. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, I trust you even in the small painful details of my life. Thank you for fulfilling every detail of the prophecy. Thank you for your precision. Help me to trust you with the details. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about clothes? Maybe a fashion designer. Maybe a tailor. Maybe a shopper. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about clothes. He spoke about garments. He spoke about casting lots. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." - Psalm 22:18 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David is describing the scene at the crucifixion. He says, "They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his clothes, dividing them into four shares, one for each of them, with the undergarment remaining. This garment was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom. 'Let's not tear it,' they said to one another. 'Let's decide by lot who will get it.' This happened that the scripture might be fulfilled..." - John 19:23-24


The soldiers gambled for the garment of Jesus. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the random actions of the soldiers. God used their random actions to fulfill His word. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Nothing that happens to you is outside of God's plan. Even the smallest details of your life are in His hands. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Thank you, God, for being in control of every detail. Even the random things in my life are under your care. Help me to trust you. Help me to rest in your sovereignty. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about loneliness? Maybe a widow. Maybe an orphan. Maybe a stranger. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about loneliness. He spoke about abandonment. He spoke about forsakenness. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, so far from my cries of anguish?" - Psalm 22:1 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David felt abandoned by God. He cried out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out in a loud voice, 'Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?' (which means 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?')." - Matthew 27:46


Jesus quoted this Psalm on the cross. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the spiritual agony of the Messiah. He would feel forsaken. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Because Jesus experienced separation from God on the cross, you will never have to. You will never be forsaken. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Thank you, Jesus, that I will never be forsaken. Thank you for experiencing separation so that I could experience acceptance. Thank you for the access I have to the Father. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a grave? Maybe a funeral director. Maybe a stone mason. Maybe a gardener. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a grave. He spoke about a rich man. He spoke about a tomb. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth." - Isaiah 53:9 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah said the Messiah would be assigned a grave with the wicked. This meant He would die among criminals. But Isaiah also said He would be with the rich in His death. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"As evening approached, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who had himself become a disciple of Jesus. Going to Pilate, he asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him. Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut out of the rock." - Matthew 27:57-60


Joseph of Arimathea buried Jesus in his own new tomb. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the burial of the Messiah. He would be buried by a rich man. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Even in death, God honored His Son. He will honor you too. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, I trust you to honor me in my life and in my death. Thank you for the hope of the resurrection. Thank you for the empty tomb. Help me to live with eternity in mind. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about resurrection? Maybe a preacher. Maybe a teacher. Maybe a believer. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about resurrection. He spoke about the grave. He spoke about decay. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will rest secure, because you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead, nor will you let your faithful one see decay." - Psalm 16:9-10 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David said God would not abandon him to the realm of the dead. He said God would not let his faithful one see decay. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Seeing what was to come, he spoke of the resurrection of the Messiah, that he was not abandoned to the realm of the dead, nor did his body see decay. God has raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it." - Acts 2:31-32


Peter preached this on the day of Pentecost. He said David knew the Messiah would rise from the dead. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is the cornerstone of the Christian faith. The tomb is empty. Jesus rose from the dead. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Death is not the end of the story. The grave is not the final word. Jesus is alive. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for defeating death. Thank you that the grave is empty. Because you live, I will live forever. Help me to live in the power of your resurrection. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a throne? Maybe a king. Maybe a queen. Maybe a ruler. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about a throne. He spoke about a kingdom. He spoke about a reign. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"When you ascended on high, you took many captives; you received gifts from people, even from the rebellious—that you, LORD God, might dwell there." - Psalm 68:18 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David described a victorious king who ascends on high. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"This is why it says: 'When he ascended on high, he took many captives and gave gifts to his people.'" - Ephesians 4:8


Paul applied this to Jesus. Jesus ascended on high. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the ascension of the Messiah. He would ascend on high. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Jesus has taken back the keys of death and hell. You have access to His victory and His gifts. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for sharing your victory with me. Thank you for the gifts you give me. Thank you for ascending on high. Help me to walk in your victory. Help me to use your gifts for your glory. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a kingdom? Maybe a politician. Maybe a president. Maybe a prime minister. Daniel was that kind of voice. He spoke about a kingdom. He spoke about a king. He spoke about a forever reign. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed." - Daniel 7:13-14 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Daniel saw a vision of one like a son of man. He was given an everlasting dominion. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, which said: 'The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever.'" - Revelation 11:15


Jesus reigns forever. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is the final prediction. The kingdom of the world becomes the kingdom of our Lord. The voice of Daniel was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The story is not just a historical mystery. It is a future reality. Jesus is coming back. He will reign forever. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, I give my life to you. Take my life and use it for your kingdom. Thank you for the hope of eternity. Thank you for the promise of a forever kingdom. Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.
pages.title: Day 16: The Voice of Daniel

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a star? Maybe an astronomer. Maybe a navigator. Maybe a dreamer. Moses was that kind of voice. He spoke about a star. He spoke about a scepter. He spoke about a king. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel." - Numbers 24:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Balaam was a pagan prophet. God used him to speak. He said a star would come out of Jacob. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


**The Fulfillment (NT


….
pages.title: Day 17: The Voice of Moses Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Fulfillment (NT)
"Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him." - Matthew 2:2


When Jesus was born, wise men came from the east. They saw a star in the sky. They knew the ancient prophecy. They traveled hundreds of miles to find Him. The star led them to Jesus. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a strange prediction. It was spoken by a nonbeliever. It connects a star to a king. The story of the wise men lines up perfectly. The voice of Balaam was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The stars themselves were pointing to a king. The universe is not silent. It speaks. It points. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, the heavens declare your glory. Thank you for putting signs in the sky that point to Jesus. Thank you for the wise men who followed the star. Help me to follow the clues that lead to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 17: The Voice of Moses Again (Continued)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a son? Maybe a father. Maybe a mother. Maybe a parent. Hosea was that kind of voice. He spoke about a son. He spoke about Egypt. He spoke about a calling. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son." - Hosea 11:1 (Written around 750 B.C.)


Hosea wrote this about the nation of Israel. God called Israel out of Egypt. But Matthew saw a deeper meaning. He saw that this verse also pointed to Jesus. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night and left for Egypt, where he stayed until the death of Herod. And so was fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: 'Out of Egypt I called my son.'" - Matthew 2:14-15


King Herod wanted to kill the baby Jesus. Joseph took Mary and Jesus and fled to Egypt. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a strange prediction. It was originally about the nation of Israel. But Matthew applies it to Jesus. Jesus is the true Israel. The voice of Hosea was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Jesus knows what it feels like to be displaced. He knows what it feels like to be afraid. He understands your fears. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for understanding what it feels like to be afraid. Thank you for being with me when I am scared. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for being my refuge. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: The Voice of Hosea

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about crying? Maybe a mourner. Maybe a griever. Maybe a mother. Jeremiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about crying. He spoke about weeping. He spoke about Rachel. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"This is what the LORD says: 'A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.'" - Jeremiah 31:15 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Jeremiah was writing about the exile of Israel. Rachel was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She was a symbol of all the mothers of Israel. The prophecy says she is weeping. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When Herod realized that he had been outwitted by the Magi, he was furious, and he gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under..." - Matthew 2:16


King Herod ordered the killing of the boys in Bethlehem. The mothers wept. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a dark prediction. It is a prediction about human evil. But even in this darkness, the prophecy was fulfilled. The voice of Jeremiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The Bible does not ignore pain. It enters into it. God is with you in your grief. He sees your tears. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, you see my tears. You know my pain. Thank you for not ignoring my suffering. Thank you for being with me in the darkness. Comfort me today. Comfort those who are grieving. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The Voice of Jeremiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a voice? Maybe a announcer. Maybe a herald. Maybe a messenger. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a voice. He spoke about a wilderness. He spoke about a way. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"A voice of one calling: 'In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.'" - Isaiah 40:3 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah wrote about a voice in the wilderness. This voice would cry out. It would tell people to prepare the way for the Lord. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea and saying, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.'" - Matthew 3:1-3


John the Baptist was that voice. He lived in the wilderness. He preached a message of repentance. He told people Jesus was coming. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
The Jews were waiting for this voice. They asked John if he was the Messiah. He said no. He said he was just a voice. Jesus was the main act. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Every spiritual awakening begins with preparation. A voice cries out. A heart gets ready. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the voices that point to Jesus. Thank you for the people who prepared the way for me to know you. Prepare my heart for what you have for me. Help me to be ready. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a servant? Maybe a helper. Maybe a healer. Maybe a hero. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a servant. He spoke about an anointed one. He spoke about a healer. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"The Spirit of the Sovereign LORD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners..." - Isaiah 61:1 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah is speaking about the Messiah. He says the Spirit of the Lord is on Him. He is anointed to heal. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He went to Nazareth... and on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue... He stood up to read... 'The Spirit of the Lord is on me...' Then he began to say to them, 'Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.'" - Luke 4:16-21


Jesus read this exact passage. He said, "Today this scripture is fulfilled." The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
Jesus quoted this passage and applied it to Himself. He was the one Isaiah wrote about. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
This is your inheritance. Jesus came to heal your broken heart. He came to set you free. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the healer. Thank you for binding up my broken heart. Thank you for setting me free from the things that hold me captive. Thank you for the good news. Heal me today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about light? Maybe a lighthouse keeper. Maybe a candle maker. Maybe a star gazer. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about light. He spoke about darkness. He spoke about Galilee. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of deep darkness a light has dawned." - Isaiah 9:2 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah said the people walking in darkness would see a great light. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum... to fulfill what was said through the prophet Isaiah... the people living in darkness have seen a great light..." - Matthew 4:13-16


Jesus moved to Capernaum. He began His ministry there. He was the light in the darkness. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a geographical prediction. It said the Messiah would bring light to Galilee. Jesus brought light to Galilee. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
God meets you where you are. No place is too dark for His light to reach. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the light in the darkness. Thank you for shining your light in the dark places. Shine your light into my heart today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a stone? Maybe a builder. Maybe a mason. Maybe an architect. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about a stone. He spoke about a cornerstone. He spoke about rejection. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the LORD has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes." - Psalm 118:22 (Written around 500 B.C.)


The builders looked at this stone and rejected it. But it became the cornerstone. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes" - Matthew 21:42


Jesus quoted this Psalm. He applied it to Himself. He was the rejected stone. He became the cornerstone. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about rejection and vindication. Jesus was rejected. He was exalted. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
When others reject you, remember that God sees your worth. You are a cornerstone. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
God, thank you that you see my worth. Thank you that you do not reject me. Thank you that Jesus was rejected so that I could be accepted. Help me to find my worth in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about hatred? Maybe a victim. Maybe a survivor. Maybe a witness. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about hatred. He spoke about enemies. He spoke about a cause. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Those who hate me without reason outnumber the hairs of my head; many are my enemies without cause, those who seek to destroy me. I am forced to restore what I did not steal." - Psalm 69:4 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was being chased by his enemies. They hated him for no reason. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: 'They hated me without reason.'" - John 15:25


Jesus said the world hated Him without a reason. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the rejection of the Messiah. He would be hated. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
If you are hated for doing the right thing, you are in good company. Jesus understands. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for enduring hatred for me. Thank you for loving me even when others hated you. Help me to love those who hate me. Help me to forgive those who hurt me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a friend? Maybe a best friend. Maybe a confidant. Maybe a companion. David was that kind of voice. He spoke about a friend. He spoke about betrayal. He spoke about bread. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." - Psalm 41:9 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was betrayed by a close friend. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I am not referring to all of you; I know those I have chosen. But this is to fulfill this passage of Scripture: 'He who shared my bread has turned against me.'" - John 13:18


Jesus was betrayed by Judas. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about intimate betrayal. The Messiah would be betrayed by someone close. The voice of David was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The greatest pain is not from enemies. It is from those we trust. Jesus understands. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for understanding the pain of betrayal. Thank you for being a friend who never betrays. Heal my heart from the wounds of broken friendships. Help me to trust again. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The Voice of David Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a price? Maybe a merchant. Maybe a buyer. Maybe a seller. Zechariah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a price. He spoke about silver. He spoke about a potter. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"I told them, 'If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it.' So they paid me thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, 'Throw it to the potter'—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD." - Zechariah 11:12-13 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah was paid thirty pieces of silver. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then one of the Twelve—the one called Judas Iscariot—went to the chief priests and asked, 'What are you willing to give me if I deliver him over to you?' So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver." - Matthew 26:14-15


Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the exact amount of money. The voice of Zechariah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Jesus allowed Himself to be valued at the price of a slave. He valued you that much. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for valuing me enough to humble yourself. Thank you for allowing yourself to be sold for thirty pieces of silver. Thank you for loving me that much. Help me to see my worth in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Voice of Zechariah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about silence? Maybe a monk. Maybe a quiet person. Maybe a listener. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about silence. He spoke about a lamb. He spoke about a trial. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth." - Isaiah 53:7 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah described the suffering servant. He was silent. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But Jesus made no reply, not even to a single charge..." - Matthew 27:14


Jesus was silent during His trial. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the behavior of the Messiah during his trial. He would be silent. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is be silent. Trusting God in the face of false accusations is strength. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being silent so that I could speak to God. Thank you for enduring false accusations. Help me to trust you when I am accused. Help me to be silent when I need to be. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a shepherd? Maybe a pastor. Maybe a guide. Maybe a protector. Zechariah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a shepherd. He spoke about a sword. He spoke about scattering. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is close to me! declares the LORD Almighty. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the little ones." - Zechariah 13:7 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah said the sword will strike the shepherd. The sheep will be scattered. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then Jesus told them, 'This very night you will all fall away on account of me, for it is written: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered."'" - Matthew 26:31


Jesus quoted this prophecy. The disciples ran away. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the disciples. They were the sheep. They would scatter. The voice of Zechariah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
Even when you fail or run away, Jesus does not abandon you. He is the Good Shepherd who goes after the scattered sheep. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for never giving up on me. Thank you for coming after me when I run away. Thank you for being the Good Shepherd. Help me to stop running. Help me to stay close to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The Voice of Zechariah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about a criminal? Maybe a judge. Maybe a lawyer. Maybe a witness. Isaiah was that kind of voice. He spoke about a criminal. He spoke about transgressors. He spoke about intercession. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death, and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors." - Isaiah 53:12 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah said the Messiah would be numbered with the transgressors. He would be crucified with criminals. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with him to be executed... they crucified him there, along with the criminals..." - Luke 23:32-33


Jesus was crucified between two criminals. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is a prediction about the method of execution. The Messiah would be crucified with criminals. The voice of Isaiah was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The innocent was treated like the guilty so the guilty could be set free. Jesus took your place. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being numbered with the criminals so I could be numbered with the saints. Thank you for forgiving me. Thank you for taking my place. Help me to forgive others. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Voice of Isaiah Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a voice that spoke about the future? Maybe a prophet. Maybe a seer. Maybe a dreamer. The Bible is full of voices that spoke about the future. They spoke about a coming king. They spoke about a coming savior. They spoke about a coming kingdom. It was the future told.


The Ancient Voice (OT)
"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed." - Daniel 7:13-14 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Daniel saw a vision of one like a son of man. He was given an everlasting dominion. This was a prediction. This was the future told.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, which said: 'The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever.'" - Revelation 11:15


Jesus reigns forever. The future was told. The future came.


The Verdict
This is the final prediction. The kingdom of the world becomes the kingdom of our Lord. The voice of Daniel was not silent. It was the future told.


The Resonance
The story is not just a historical mystery. It is a future reality. Jesus is coming back. He will reign forever. The future is not random. It is told.


The Prayer
Jesus, I give my life to you. Take my life and use it for your kingdom. Thank you for the hope of eternity. Thank you for the promise of a forever kingdom. Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.



END MATTER


The 300+ Prophecy Challenge
We only looked at 30 prophecies in this book. The Bible contains over 300 prophecies about Jesus. If you want to keep investigating, I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It tells the story of Jesus from the perspective of an eyewitness. As you read, look for the clues. Look for the prophecies. Look for the evidence. You will be amazed at what you find.


The Probability Factor
Mathematicians have calculated the probability of one person fulfilling just eight of these prophecies. The odds are 1 in 10 to the 17th power. That is a one with seventeen zeros after it. That is the same as covering the entire state of Texas with silver coins, marking one coin, and having a blindfolded person pick the right coin on the first try. Jesus fulfilled not eight. Not thirty. Over three hundred. The math points to a miracle.


A Note on Faith
Evidence is important. It satisfies the mind. But evidence does not save you. The evidence points to a person. The evidence points to Jesus. You can believe the facts and still be far from God. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The evidence is on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the evidence that the Bible is true. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.

If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Ultimate Evidence takes a 30 day look at 30 messianic prophecies and their stunning fulfillments. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.
